summary: Step 1 of scripts/pre-pr-check.sh is not merely mislabelled -- its sorry-detection logic is a verbatim duplicate of check-sorry-suppressions.sh's count_sorries(), and its entire 24-hit/6-file failure set is already present, per file and exactly (7,2,12,1,1,1), in scripts/sorry-suppression-baseline.txt, whose scan root (Cslib) is a strict superset of step 1's four hand-picked trees. So the task's option (a) 'add a frozen per-file baseline' is not a new gate to build -- it already exists as step 8, and reuse means DELEGATION, not a second baseline. Second decisive finding: option (b) alone provably does not work -- measured against merge-base with origin/main, 114 in-scope .lean files are changed and 3 of the 6 debt files (SuccRelation, UntilSinceCoherence, Frame) are among them, so a changed-files gate that still fails on ANY sorry reproduces the same wall. Recommendation: step 1 delegates to check-sorry-suppressions.sh via a new --scope filter (preserves step numbering, so zero renumbering of the 7 external 'step N of pre-pr-check.sh' citations), with --changed as an opt-in extra narrowing. Blast radius is low: pre-pr-check.sh is fork-local (absent from upstream/main), is not wired into either CI workflow or the /pr 7-step pipeline, and the 'passes end to end' completion bar is per-plan prose with no template in agent-system/extensions/cslib. Highest-risk implementation trap identified: a scoped --update would rewrite the whole-tree baseline from a partial sweep and silently zero the out-of-scope Propositional/Tableau rows -- must exit 2.
decisions_made: RECOMMENDED DESIGN (Option 1): step 1 becomes a scoped invocation of check-sorry-suppressions.sh via a new '--scope PATH...' filter, passing the same four trees. Chosen over authoring a per-file baseline inside pre-pr-check.sh because that baseline already exists (sorry-suppression-baseline.txt) and a second one would be a strict-subset duplicate that can never fail where step 8 passes.

Step numbering is DELIBERATELY PRESERVED. Seven external sites cite pre-pr-check.sh steps by number (scripts/README.md:57/83/101, docs/lint-suppression-policy.md:11, and header comments in check-sorry-suppressions.sh:62, check-shake-residue.sh:41, check-axiom-census.sh:46). Option 2 (delete step 1, renumber 2-9 to 1-8, move the sorry ratchet to the front) is technically the cleanest end state and strictly more coverage, but was rejected on the 7-site renumbering cost; recorded in the report as a considered alternative rather than dropped.

--changed is specified as an OPT-IN flag defaulting OFF in pre-pr-check.sh, not as the primary mechanism, because the measurement shows it does not fix satisfiability on its own and because defaulting it on would make a local gate's result depend on git state.

Default base ref for --changed is origin/main, not upstream/main: merge-base with upstream/main yields 626 changed .lean files (this fork has diverged substantially), which is useless as a filter. origin/main yields 132 (114 in-scope).

No agent-system/extensions/** change is in scope. Grep of agent-system/extensions/cslib/, .claude/skills/skill-cslib-*/ and .claude/agents/cslib-*.md found zero occurrences of 'pre-pr-check' or an equivalent completion-bar template -- every citation is per-task prose under specs/. The source-store/deploy-boundary rule is not engaged either, since scripts/ is a real tracked repo directory, not a .claude/** deploy artifact.

Both declared non-goals upheld and restated as plan guardrails: step 5 (lake build --wfail --iofail) is untouched, and no file under Cslib/ is edited (no sorry is resolved). sorry-suppression-baseline.txt must remain byte-identical -- the ratchet is currently exactly at baseline (18/18 markers, 28/28 sorries, verified this dispatch).
dead_ends: Implementing a second, step-1-local frozen sorry baseline (the literal reading of the task's option (a)): rejected. check-sorry-suppressions.sh's baseline already contains step 1's failure set exactly, over a superset scan root, using byte-identical discrimination logic; a second baseline would duplicate the rule the existing script's header explicitly says not to weaken, and could never report a failure step 8 misses.

A changed-files mode that still fails on ANY sorry (option (b) with the original predicate): empirically disproven this dispatch. 3 of the 6 debt-carrying files (Bundle/SuccRelation.lean, Bundle/UntilSinceCoherence.lean, BXCanonical/Frame.lean) are inside the changed set vs merge-base with origin/main, so the gate would still be unsatisfiable for any task touching them -- the same wall, narrower.
A changed-files DELTA gate (fail when a changed file exceeds its baseline entry): strictly weaker than step 8, which already applies that predicate to every file in Cslib. No unique signal.
upstream/main as the --changed base ref: 626 changed .lean files, no filtering value.

Copying check-lint-suppressions.sh's $-anchored blanket-only regex or its exact-set shape from check-shake-residue.sh: both are the wrong shape here (counts vs set membership), and check-sorry-suppressions.sh's own header already documents why the anchored form must NOT be copied to the sorry gate (all 18 markers on this tree are the declaration-scoped '... false in' form, so an anchored regex would count 0).
